subject.title: Unhandled Playwright assertion error in CRSession._onMessage crashes Gateway

question: Should OpenClaw handle Playwright CDP assertion leakage with a narrow browser-owned recovery/classifier, or should this wait for a broader browser subprocess isolation design?
rationale: The source path is clear enough to keep the issue open, but choosing between targeted suppression, reconnect semantics, and process isolation changes the Gateway crash boundary and cannot be settled safely by automation without live repro evidence.

options.title: Require live repro, then add browser-owned recovery
options.body: Capture the CRSession CDP message path first, then implement the narrowest browser-owned handler that logs, tears down the affected Playwright connection, and keeps the Gateway alive.

options.title: Design subprocess isolation first
options.body: Pause code repair until maintainers define a browser worker/process boundary that can crash independently from the Gateway.

options.title: Defer until another production repro
options.body: Leave the issue open but do not spend implementation time until a current-main log or reproduction identifies the exact CDP message shape.

recommendation.title: Require live repro, then add browser-owned recovery
recommendation.body: Capture the CRSession CDP message path first, then implement the narrowest browser-owned handler that logs, tears down the affected Playwright connection, and keeps the Gateway alive.

likelyOwner.reason: He appears most connected to both the browser CDP session path and the global unhandled rejection architecture.
